pull_request.title: Calorimeter: design a common forward calorimeter for both layouts
pull_request.head: codex/common-fcal-design
pull_request.body:
The two layout candidates reserve forward space without a physical FCAL/readout design. This proposes a common 1.8 m tungsten/quartz-fibre body with rear SiPM readout, plus the short EM collar needed for the LAr layout. DES-039 and ADR-010 retain the source evidence, exact placements, material/readout/power budgets and updated R–Z views for both candidates.

The proposal explicitly changes the empty bore allocation from R80 to R50 mm and adds the collar collector, R298 mm service neck and rear handoff planes. It remains an isolated DRAFT / PROTOTYPE: the downstream machine interface, complete optical/service networks, shower response, radiation lifetime and engineering qualification remain open.

Validation:

- Eleven geometry, packing, conservation, identifier, adverse and report-format controls pass. The retained report uses twelve significant digits with a strict byte comparison; full-precision physical calculations and native tolerances are unchanged.
- ROOT constructs both signs in both layouts, including the 02 collar and straight service neck: zero overlaps at 1e-5 mm; 72 IP rays and 18 axial controls agree with analytical paths.
- Separate PhysVal assessment of the fixed scientific revision found no blocking issue for the scoped envelope fit; two minor dossier wording/allocation issues are corrected. A separate follow-up review confirmed that portable report serialization changes no physical conclusion or tolerance.
- Native ROOT covers the FCAL component and conservative neighbour guards. Detailed fan-out, curved collector connections, DD4hep/readout integration and Geant4 transport are not claimed.

Artifacts and accounting:

- [LAYOUT-001 3D cutaway SVG](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/common-fcal-design/docs/design/figures/DES-039/LAYOUT-001-FCAL-3d.svg) and [eight-sentence technology summary](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/common-fcal-design/docs/design/figures/DES-039/LAYOUT-001-FCAL-summary.txt).
- [Exact token recovery audit](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/common-fcal-design/logs/usage/USAGE-2026-10-20-pr88-accounting.json): 11 completed turns across the parent chat and four specialist children, 40,048,091 input + 215,814 output = 40,263,905 observed tokens. The SVG turn accounts for 2,583,296 of these tokens. Cached/reasoning subsets are not added twice; the active accounting/readiness turn remains excluded.
- Main merged normally, preserving the FCAL and ODD IdRes tasks, both CI checks, sources and journals. Geometry, figures and native validation evidence are unchanged. No design sign-off or production acceptance is implied.

The two layout candidates reserve forward space without a physical FCAL/readout design. This proposes a common 1.8 m tungsten/quartz-fibre body with rear SiPM readout, plus the short EM collar needed for the LAr layout. DES-039 and ADR-010 retain the source evidence, exact placements, material/readout/power budgets and updated R–Z views for both candidates.

The proposal explicitly changes the empty bore allocation from R80 to R50 mm and adds the collar collector, R298 mm service neck and rear handoff planes. It remains an isolated DRAFT / PROTOTYPE: the downstream machine interface, complete optical/service networks, shower response, radiation lifetime and engineering qualification remain open.

Validation:

- Eleven geometry, packing, conservation, identifier, adverse and report-format controls pass. The retained report uses twelve significant digits with a strict byte comparison; full-precision physical calculations and native tolerances are unchanged.
- ROOT constructs both signs in both layouts, including the 02 collar and straight service neck: zero overlaps at 1e-5 mm; 72 IP rays and 18 axial controls agree with analytical paths.
- Separate PhysVal assessment of the fixed scientific revision found no blocking issue for the scoped envelope fit; two minor dossier wording/allocation issues are corrected. A separate follow-up review confirmed that portable report serialization changes no physical conclusion or tolerance.
- Native ROOT covers the FCAL component and conservative neighbour guards. Detailed fan-out, curved collector connections, DD4hep/readout integration and Geant4 transport are not claimed.

Artifacts and accounting:

- [LAYOUT-001 3D cutaway SVG](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/common-fcal-design/docs/design/figures/DES-039/LAYOUT-001-FCAL-3d.svg) and [eight-sentence technology summary](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/common-fcal-design/docs/design/figures/DES-039/LAYOUT-001-FCAL-summary.txt).

The SVG turn accounts for 2,583,296 of these tokens. Cached/reasoning subsets are not added twice; the active accounting/readiness turn remains excluded.

User request: “Ok, also do the token accounting for this one, resolve merge conflict - and make it ready to merge.” This author follow-up began at `3818a0712dbadcdca256c077b9ce5a0db4ee7838`, with a clean FCAL worktree. PR88 was open and non-draft but conflicting with main; no reviews or inline comments were present. No merge or auto-merge was requested or performed.

Applied the repository review-validation procedure and SoftEng mandate under author assignment PR88-READINESS-2026-10-20. Inputs are the exact starting head, main `969a870`, existing DES039/ADR010 and validation records, the usage-only recovery tool and current PR metadata. [**3D cutaway SVG**]([redacted] · [PNG preview]([redacted]

Tungsten provides substantial absorber depth within the narrow forward envelope. ([PDG](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/AtomicNuclearProperties/HTML/tungsten_W.html))  
Quartz fibres provide Cherenkov light and radiation tolerance, following established CMS forward-calorimeter experience. ([CMS HF]([external URL redacted; see source journal]))  
Rear fibre extraction places compact readout and cooling in the available downstream space.

Each module is **1.80 m long**, with a **580 mm outer diameter** and **100 mm central bore**, positioned at |z| = **4.533–6.333 m**.  
The **1.20 m sampling block** contains **24,324 fused-silica fibres** with 0.6 mm cores on a 3 mm lattice.  
Interleaved long and short fibres provide overlapping depth weightings, with short fibres starting 100 mm deeper.  
Sixteen azimuthal sectors and three radial bands produce **96 tower signals per end**, read by cooled SiPM arrays behind a 300 mm optical fan-out.

The cutaway enlarges representative fibres for clarity, and the design remains a prototype awaiting machine, radiation, shower and engineering qualification.  
SVG rendering and all **11 FCAL checks passed**.

events.text:
Assignment **FCAL-PhysVal-01** reviewed exact commit **`3c5eded29c1186e7dbd213ac5aab913376babc05`**, read-only. No files changed; no further delegation.

The evidence supports the **scoped prototype envelope-fit claim**: the common body fits the two pinned layout contexts, with the additional 02 collar and explicitly declared aperture/service amendments. I found **no blocking numerical or scientific interpretation error** in that claim. It does not establish a complete installed or functioning calorimeter.

Minor corrections recommended:

- **P3 — stale radial allocation:** `docs/design/inputs/DES-039-fcal-technology.md:59` retains R270–276 mm support and R276–288 mm service intervals; the authoritative inputs/native geometry use the sampling-shell boundary at **R278 mm**. Update the dossier or explicitly mark those earlier allocations superseded.
- **P3 — ambiguous transform wording:** the same file at line **77** says the negative assembly is “reflected.” Replace this with **proper Rx(180°) rotation**. The implementation and its determinant check are already correct.

The important open limits are accurately disclosed in DES039 and the results:

- The **R50 mm bore** replaces R80 mm; the pipe is only described to |z| = 4 m. Machine clearance remains unqualified.
- Collar local coolant lines at R444 mm, the R435→294 mm collector, its connections and full manifolds are not a completed continuous native network. `results.md:67` correctly states the omission.
- Long/short fibres provide overlapping depth weightings, rather than independent EM/HAD compartments.
- Material paths, fibre crossings and average nuclear λ do not establish optical response, efficiency, containment or pion interaction length.
- The phase grid excludes aligned seams; explicit zero-matrix seam controls preserve that adverse result.
- Optical loom collisions, shower/edge leakage, radiation lifetime, beam heat, electronics, thermal/hydraulic, structural and access qualification remain open.

Actual checks:

- Read the pinned inputs using `git show`.
- Verified analytical input/model/context hashes and all native executed-source hashes against the reviewed commit: **all match**.
- Compared both context snapshots with their exact historical source fields: **no differences**.
- Ran `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/forward_calorimeter -p 'test_*.py' -v`: **10/10 pass**; current scientific files were first verified byte-identical to the reviewed commit.
- Independently solved line–finite-cylinder intersections using distance-parameter quadratics for **38 random/adverse body/collar rays**: worst discrepancy **1.11 × 10⁻⁹ mm**.
- Independently reconstructed finite tungsten volumes and confirmed the partial masses: **4840.200 kg/body/end**, **1105.167 kg/collar/end**.
- Independently confirmed nominal/adverse heat and ideal 3 K flows: **109.472/458.488 W** and **0.008722/0.036527 kg/s** per component/end.
- Verified tungsten/silica reference values and sensor package/pixel geometry against [PDG tungsten](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/AtomicNuclearProperties/HTML/tungsten_W.html), [PDG fused quartz](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2020/AtomicNuclearProperties/HTML/silicon_dioxide_fused_quartz.html), and the [manufacturer datasheet]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

I inspected the retained native reports; I did **not** rerun ROOT, DD4hep, Geant4 or Spack. Their recorded successful exits, zero reported overlaps and path residuals are consistent with the reviewed source hashes and disclosed scope.

This is an independent AI technical assessment, not human design approval or acceptance.
